rated_messages.input_message: Ask yourself, "From 0-10, how willing am I to let this urge pass without smoking?" Let it pass to be closer to the things that matter most to you.
Step back from what is stressful by taking 10 slow breaths. Count them as you go and notice your breath. If you get distracted, keep starting over until you get to 10.
Ways of dealing with urges: play a game or an online quiz.
If you're stuck at home and physical activity doesn't interest you, try gaming, needlework, drawing, or journaling.
What inspires you most to quit smoking? Are you willing to let this urge pass without smoking for that reason?
Notice what it feels like to see other people smoke and choose not to smoke. Notice what thoughts or emotions come up. Allow them to come and go. They will pass and so will this urge.
Instead of smoking, think of 3 things from today that you are grateful for. These can be anything, even small things! Now ask yourself, why are you grateful for these things?
Are you feeling down because you are thinking of smoking? It's really important to be kind to yourself, and to make sure you give yourself praise too!
Crumple a piece of paper into a ball and imagine it is your urge. Toss the "urge" into the garbage or against the wall. By doing this, you are letting go of your urges.
Try chewing gum if you have trouble resisting smoking when other people light up around you.
